duplicate_owner_check.evidence: createRecoverySpell uses tload/tstore(owner,1) for dedup (L62-70) but NEVER clears the transient slots after the loop; calculateAddress uses a clean O(n^2) loop (L97-103)

param_checks.evidence: _paramChecks covers threshold/zero/delay, not cross-call transient state

invariant_analysis.broken_invariant: the duplicate-owner check must be scoped to a single createRecoverySpell call; transient state must not leak across calls in a tx
invariant_analysis.why_defenses_do_not_block: no clearing of transient storage between/after calls

exploit_path.attacker_profile: any deployer / orchestrator (multicall) creating >1 spell in one tx
exploit_path.preconditions: two createRecoverySpell calls in the SAME transaction whose owner sets share >=1 address
exploit_path.transaction_sequence: call 1 sets tstore(ownerO,1) and never clears it; call 2 (different safe/spell) containing ownerO reads tload(ownerO)=1 -> require(!found) reverts 'Duplicate owner' even though ownerO is not a duplicate WITHIN call 2's set. Same-tx batch creation of spells sharing any owner reverts.
exploit_path.state_after: second creation reverts on a false duplicate
exploit_path.rejection_case: Real (transient slots are tx-scoped and never cleared here, unlike the view calculateAddress). Severity is the open question: it is a liveness/DoS of a SECURITY mechanism's batched setup, but a separate-tx workaround exists and there is no direct fund loss -> bounded. Defer the bounded-vs-material call to the isolated adversarial review.
exploit_path.source_evidence: RecoverySpellFactory.createRecoverySpell L59-71 (tload/tstore dedup, no clear); cf. calculateAddress L97-103 (clean loop)

impact_analysis.impact_category: DoS of batched recovery-spell deployment (false duplicate across same-tx calls)
impact_analysis.minimum_profit_or_damage_condition: any same-tx multi-spell deployment with a shared owner reverts; workaround = separate txs
